goal: Sustained wall-clock useful-work coverage >=93.33% with substantive durable-evidence gaps <=120s.

active_interventions.expected_effect: Suppress voluntary objective-complete return; cannot physically prevent invocation disappearance.
Deny normal final while nonterminal authority remains; future cold wake is not end authority.
Replace fixed-quarter scheduler loss with provisional bounded rescue and completion-relative fast reentry while retaining one canonical.
Provide independent replacement path and stronger SaaS-grade resilience.
Best-effort liveness rescue only; not a <=120s path.

live_interpretation: Historical fixed-quarter evidence established a 483-second replacement gap after physical invocation loss. A later controlled two-wake test proved the same hourly RRULE canonical can move DTSTART forward and wake again automatically. Production has therefore migrated to a rolling lifecycle: provisional arm before work, then completion-relative final rearm. The first production rolling wake is now active; no rolling acceptance window is counted until its full lifecycle and next automatic wake are observed.
dominant_risks: Canary success may not generalize to a long production invocation.
A final-rearm mutation failure near normal close could leave only the slower provisional rescue; this must be measured, not hidden.
No independent event consumer is provisioned, so same-canonical scheduler behavior remains a single-provider dependency.
Acceptance accounting must not mix historical fixed-quarter samples with rolling samples without normalization.
next_decision: Complete the first production rolling lifecycle observation, measure actual final-rearm-to-next-wake gap and any stale/duplicate behavior, then collect three audited rolling windows. Pursue independent event wake as resilience work after or alongside rolling validation when it does not compromise P0 measurement.
